newsitem.title: ALBANIA: EU opens monitoring office in southern Albania.
newsitem.headline: EU opens monitoring office in southern Albania.

text.p: A European Union monitoring mission has opened an office in southern Albania to observe the post-election situation in the Balkan country, EU officials said on Friday.

The move comes after the international community pledged to help Albania rebuild itself socially, politically, economically and militarily after the collapse of bogus investment schemes stripped thousands of their life savings and threw the country into chaos.

A six-member EU team headed by Dutch diplomat Ton de Vaan will operate from the town of Gjirokaster, 230 km (140 miles) south of Tirana, close to the Greek border. The assignment is for an indefinite period.
"We will monitor economic, political, military, and security developments and ... Brussels will be the headquarters for assessing Albania's needs and assistance," de Vaan told Reuters.

A conference held last month in Rome by some 35 countries and world institutions promised to help Albania rebuild itself, but urged the new government to restore public order, improve human rights and adopt sound economic policies.
The collapse of shaky pyramid investment schemes swallowed the life savings of tens of thousands of Albanians and triggered months of violent unrest in which more than 1,500 people were killed.
The unrest lead to the fall of the government of former President Sali Berisha who was eventually replaced by Socialist Prime Minister Fatos Nano in elections in June.
